## Test strategy

Guardian: `cd packages/guardian && bun test` (package.json script `test: bun test --no-orphans`). The CORS suite (src/cors.test.ts) is the template: it spawns the real guardian via `Bun.spawn(['bun','run','src/server.ts'])` with env-injected ports/allowlist and asserts real HTTP responses — extend it only if the default allowlist gains the hosted origin. Client: `cd packages/client && bun test` (unit, tests/*.test.ts) — write the HTTPS-refusal tests first, modeled on tests/transport-health-cors.test.ts (transport behavior) and tests/connections-page-markup.test.ts (static markup/source assertions, which is how the CORS remediation copy is already pinned, including greps of the .svelte source for env-var names — the same technique can pin the TLS-guide deep-link). Playwright e2e (`cd packages/client && npm run test:e2e`, e2e/connections-form.pw.ts) for form-level refusal if browser-context behavior matters. Compose/doc invariants: `cd packages/lib && bun test src/control-plane/assistant-client-compose.test.ts` already asserts the GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS default shape and that environment-and-mounts.md documents both env vars — update these expectations in the same commit as any compose/default change. The Tailscale/Caddy paths themselves are docs/overlay work verifiable only by manual smoke (release-management.md line 198 already includes a hosted-PWA/CORS release checklist item).

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #435 (guardian auth) — coordination, not blocking: the client-side refusal implements this issue's '#435 credentials only ever sent over HTTPS for non-loopback targets' clause; guardian Basic auth on direct ingress already exists (packages/guardian/src/auth.ts), so only the credential-attach policy in the client transport needs to agree with #435's final Bearer/Basic seam.
- #488 (mDNS) — coordination, not blocking: mDNS advertisement should surface the guardian's HTTPS (ts.net/domain) name when the TLS front is enabled; the mDNS mechanism (opencode server.mdns, referenced in packages/skeleton/system/stack/core.compose.yml:171) is #488's surface.
- #511 (PWA install paths) — reverse dependency: #511's mobile half is blocked on this issue; the only forward interaction is that baking https://app.openpalm.dev into the default CORS allowlist is meaningless until #511's hosted deploy exists, so that sub-item can trail #511.

## Risks

- The 'baked-in hosted origin' scope item may conflict with a deliberate security posture: review 2026-07-10 finding I4 was fixed by defaulting the allowlist to LOCAL client origins only, and GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS still defaults to false — silently adding app.openpalm.dev to every install's allowlist widens the browser-reachable surface before the hosted origin even exists; needs an explicit decision.
- Client-side HTTPS refusal must not break the two legitimate plain-HTTP paths: loopback targets from any origin, and plain-HTTP LAN guardians from a loopback-installed client (the PNA-trusted tier the plan §6.10 explicitly preserves) — an over-eager check would regress the zero-TLS desktop default.
- Tailscale/Caddy sidecar integration touches the compose stack and rootless-container work; if scoped as code (not just docs) it can balloon — the issue marks the sidecar as optional, so scoping discipline is needed to keep this M.
- TLS termination in front of the guardian changes the Origin/Host seen by direct ingress; the exact-origin CORS matcher (config.ts normalizeExactOrigin) must be verified against the ts.net/custom-domain origin, and the allowlist docs must tell users to add that origin.
- Credentials stored in IndexedDB over a plain-HTTP LAN client (review finding E7/I3) is adjacent but unresolved; shipping the refusal UX only in the hosted client while the LAN-served client keeps sending Basic auth over HTTP could be misread as this issue being 'done'.

## Original issue body

# #557: Guardian edge TLS + CORS for remote clients (Phase 6.5 — gates the phone/PWA story)

## Summary

Give the guardian edge an HTTPS story and a CORS allowlist so remote clients (the hosted PWA at the official URL, and any phone) can connect. This is Phase 6.5 of `docs/technical/ui-runtime-modes-plan.md` and a **hard prerequisite for the mobile half of #511**.

## Why this is unavoidable (platform rules, not our code)

- **Secure context:** a PWA installs only over HTTPS or from `localhost`. Plain HTTP on a LAN IP is never installable.
- **Mixed content:** an HTTPS origin (the hosted client) cannot `fetch()` a plain-HTTP guardian. So *every* phone → guardian connection needs TLS, regardless of where the client was installed from.
- The **desktop/localhost** install path needs none of this — a `http://127.0.0.1` origin is a secure context and may call plain-HTTP LAN guardians (loopback is the most-trusted Private Network Access tier). That's why it's the zero-setup default and this issue only gates the remote/phone story.

Today there is no TLS anywhere in the stack (verified: no caddy/tls references in `packages/skeleton/system/stack/` or `containers/`) and guardian sends no CORS headers.

## Simplicity guardrail (from the ratified plan, §8 rule 11)

**TLS is never a manual user task on default paths.** Explicit non-goal: asking non-technical users to install a private CA on iOS/Android (mkcert-style). The chosen flows must be guided.

## Scope

- [ ] **Recommended default: Tailscale.** Guided docs + (optionally) a sidecar/serve integration so a guardian gets a `ts.net` name with a real Let's Encrypt cert — no cert management for the user
- [ ] **Alternative: Caddy front** for the guardian with a user-owned domain (DNS-challenge Let's Encrypt) for users who don't want Tailscale
- [ ] **CORS allowlist** on guardian ingress: official hosted origin (e.g. `app.openpalm.dev`) baked in, additional origins configurable; enforced tests
- [ ] `requiresHttpsForRemoteConnections` enforced client-side too: the hosted client refuses plain-HTTP non-loopback targets with an actionable message deep-linking to the TLS guide
- [ ] Coordinate with #488 (mDNS advertisement should surface the HTTPS name when enabled) and #435 (credentials only ever sent over HTTPS for non-loopback targets)

## Non-goals

- No change to the loopback-default posture: guardian stays LAN-dark unless explicitly exposed (`OP_BIND_ADDRESS` policy unchanged)
- No public-internet exposure guidance beyond the Tailscale/Caddy paths
